尽管教育作为人们之所以同意任何意见的一个谬误的根据而遭到哲学的拒斥，但是教育仍然在世界上颇为流行，这就是所有的体系在最初被看作是新寄的和不寻常而容易被否定的原因。
我在这里提出的关于信念的意见或许就要遭到这样的命运，虽然在我看来我所展示的证明是完全无可置疑的，我并不期望我的意见将招来许多新的皈依者。很难使人们相信：如此重要的结果乃
①我们可以大体而言，既然我们所有的或然性推理都是建立在观念的活泼性的基础上面的，所以它就同许多被蔑视为想象的产物面遭到拒绝的那些奇想和偏见相类似。根据这种表达，想象这一语词看起来通常有两种不向的意义；尽管对于真正的暂学面言，没有什么比这种不精确更为相反的了。然面，在下面的推理中，我又常常被迫陷人这种不精确中。当我把想象和记忆相对的时候，我意指我们形成微弱观念的那个感官能力；当我将想象和理性相对的时候，我意指相同的感官能力，仅仅排除了我们证实的或者或然的推理；当我不将想象和二者相对，则无论是在更大的或更有限的意义上来理解它都无关紧要，或者至少是根据上下文就足以解释这种意义。

of such consequence can flow from principles, which are seemingly so
inconsiderable, and that the far greatest part of our reasonings, with
all our actions and passions, can be deriv′ d from nothing but custom
and habit. To obviate this objection, 1 shall here anticipate a little
what wou′ d more properly fall under our consideration afterwards,
when we come to treat of the passions and the sense of beauty.
There is implanted in the: human mind a perception of pain and
pleasure, as the chief spring and moving principle of all its actions.
But pain and pleasure have two ways of making their appearance in
the mind; of which the one has effects very different from the other.
They may either appear in inapression to the actual feeling, or only in
idea, as at present when I mention them. 'Tis evident the influence of
these upon our actions is far fromi being equal. Impressions always ac-
tuate the soul, and that in the highest degree; but'tis not every idea
which has the same effect. Nature has proceeded with caution in this
case, and seems to have carefully avoided the inconveniences of two
extremes. Did impressions alone influence the will , we should every,
moment of our lives be subject to the greatest calamities; because,
tho’we foresaw their approach, we should not beprovided by nature
with any principle of action, which might impel us to avoid them. On
the other hand, did every idea influence our actions, our condition
would not be much mended. For such is the unsteadiness and activity
of thought, that the images of every thing, especially of goods and e-
vils, are always wandering in the mind; and were it mov′ d by every
idle conception of this kind, it would never enjoy a moment’s peace
and tranquillity.
Nature has, therefore, chosen a medium, and has neither be-
stow'd on every idea of good and evil the power of actuating the
will, nor yet has entirely excluded them from this influence. Tho'
an idle fiction has no efficacy, yet we find by experience, that the
ideas of those objects, which we believe either are or will be exist-
ent, produce in a lesser degree the same effect with those impres-
sions, which are immediately present to the senses and perception.
The effect, then, of belief is to raise up a simple idea to an equality

是由看起来相当不足取的原理产生的，而且我们的绝大部分推理，以及我们的全部行动和情感，都仅仅只是源自于习惯和习性。
为了避免这种反驳，在这里我将稍微提前阐述一下我们在后面论及情感和美感时才恰当地归人我们的考察范围的几个观点。
人类的心灵已经被注入了一种痛苦和快乐的知觉，以此作为它的全部活动的主要动力和推动原理。但是，痛苦和快乐有两种不同的方式出现在心灵中，这两种方式的作用十分不同。痛苦和快乐可以是出现在印象中的真实感觉，也可以仅仅出现在观念中，正如我现在提及它们的这样。显而易见，这两种知觉对我们行动的影响是极为不同的。印象总是激起心灵，而且是最高程度的激起；但是并不是每一个观念都有同样的作用。在这种情况下，自然谨慎地处理着，而且看起来小心地避免了两个极端的不方便之处。如果单单是印象影响意志，那么我们一生中的每一时刻都将遭受到最大的灾难；因为即使我们预知了灾难的来临，自然也不会提供给我们任何可以推动我们去躲避灾难的行动的原则。另一方面，如果每一个观念都影响我们的行动，那么我们的状况将得不到更多的改善。因为人们的思想是如此的摇摆和活跃，以至每一事物、特别是善和恶的想象总是游荡在心灵中；并且如果心灵为每一个这样闲散的概念所驱使，它就决不会享受到片刻的安宁和平静。
因此，自然已经选择了一条中间路线，既不赋予善恶观念以激起意志的能力，也不完全将它们的这种影响排除在外。尽管一个无聊的虚构没有功效，然而我们通过经验发现，我们相信现在存在或将要存在的那些对象的观念，要比直接呈现于感官和知觉的那些印象产生出更小程度的相同作用。因此，信念的作用就是将一

with our impressions, and bestow on it a like influence on the pas-
sions. This effect it can only have by making an idea approach an im-
pression in force and vivacity. For as the different degrees of force
make all the original difference betwixt an impression and an idea,
they must of consequence be the source of all the differences in the
effects of these perceptions, and their removal, in whole or in part,
the cause of every new resemblance they acquire. Wherever we can
make an idea approach the impressions in force and vivacity, it will
likewise imitate them in its influence on the mind; and uice versa,
where it imitates them in that influence, as in the present case, this
must proceed from its approaching them in force and vivacity. Belief,
therefore, since it causes an idea to imitate the effects of the impres-
sions, must make it resemble them in these qualities, and is nothing
but a more vivid and intense conception of any idea. This, then, may
both serve as an additional argument for the present system, and may
give us a notion after what manner our reasonings from causation are
able to operate on the will and passions,
As belief is almost absolutely requisite to the exciting our pas-
sions , so the passions in their turn are very favourable to belief; and
not only such facts as convey agreeable emotions, but very often
such as give pain, do upon that account become more readily the ob-
jects of faith and opinion. A coward, whose fears are easily
awaken’ d, readily assents to every account of danger he meels with;
as a person of a sorrowful and melancholy disposition is very credui-
ous of every thing that nourishes his prevailing passion. When any af-
fecting object is presented, it gives the alarm, and excites immedi-
ately a degree of itsproper passion; especially in persons who are
naturally inclined to that passion. This emotion passes by an easy
transition to the imagination; and diffusing itself over our idea of the
affecting object, makes us form that idea with greater force and vivac-
ity , and consequently assent to it, according to the precedent system.

个简单观念提升到同我们的印象相等的位置，并且赋予它与情感一样的相同的影响。只有使一个观念在力度和活泼性上接近于一个印象，信念才能产生这种作用。因为既然一个印象和一个观念的全部原初的差异就在于它们的力度的不同，所以力度的不同也必定是这些知觉的作用各不相同的根源，而将这些不同的力度全部或部分去除，就成了这些知觉获得每一种新的类似关系的原因。无论什么情况下，只要我们能使一个观念在力度和活泼性上接近于一个印象，观念对心灵的影响就同印象类似。反之亦然，
在它们对心灵的影响类似的地方，正如目前这种情形，必定是由于它们在力度和活泼性上彼此接近的缘故。因此，既然信念导致了一个观念的作用同一个印象类似，所以它就必定会导致它们在性质上相类似，因而它就仅仅是对任何观念的一种更生动和强烈的构想。由此，这种既可以作为目前这个体系的一个额外的论证，又可以使我们认识到，在何种方式下，我们根据因果关系而进行的推理才能对意志和情感产生作用。
正如对刺激我们的情感而言信念几乎是绝对不可缺少的一样，因此，情感对信念也是非常有利的；不仅仅像传达惬意的情绪那样的事实，而且还常常有像给予人痛苦那样的事实，都是由于那个缘故才更容易成为信念和意见的对象。一个容易感到畏惧的儒夫，一遇到可能有的危险情况，他就会马上反应；正如一个性情悲伤和优郁的人非常轻信于能滋养他的主导情感的每一件事情。当任何感人的对象被呈现出来时，它就会发出警报，并且立刻激起在一定程度上与之相应的情感。特别是对那些天然倾向于那种情感的人来说，情况更是如此。根据先前的理论体系，这种情绪能通过一种很轻松的过渡移至想象中；并且将它

Admiration and surprize have the same effect as the othrers passi
and accordingly we may observe, that among the vulgar, quacks and
projectors meet with a more easy faith upon account of their magnifi-
cent pretensions, than if they kept themselves within the bounds of
moderation. The first astonishment, which naturally attends their mi-
raculous relations, spreads itself over the whole soul, and so vivifies
and enlivens the idea, that it resembles the inferences we draw from
experience. This is a mystery, with which we may be already a little
acquainted, and which we shall have farther occasion to be let into in
the progress of this treatise.
After this account of the influence of belief on the passions, we
shall find less difficulty in explaining its effects on the imagination,
however extraordinary they may appear. ‘Tis certain we cannot take
pleasure in any discourse, where our judgment gives no assent to
those images which are presented to our fancy. The conversation of
those, who have acquir' d a habit of lying, tho′ in affairs of no mo-
ment, never gives any satisfaction; and that because those ideas they
present to us, not being attended with belief, make no impression up-
on the mind. Poets themselves, tho′ liars by profession, always en-
deavour to give an air of truth to their fictions; and where that is total-

ble to afford much pleasure. In short, we may observe, that even
when ideas have no manner of influence on the will and passions,
truth and reality are still requisite, in order to make them entertaining
to the imagination.
But if we compare together all the phaenomena that occur on this
head, we shall find, that truth, however necessary it may seem in all
works of genius, has no other effect than to procure an easy reception for
the ideas, and to make the mind acquiesce in them with satisfaction, or
at least without reluctance. But as this is an effect, which may easily be

散布在我们的那些感人的对象的观念上，使我们能以更大的力度和活泼性形成那一观念，并因此同意它。钦佩和异同其他情感有着同样的作用；因此，我们可以看到，医和骗子在大肆吹嘘的时候，要比他们在采取谦和的态度时更容易得到普通人的信任。
由他们关马行空的胡乱联系而自然引发的最初的惊讶遍布于人的整个心灵中，并且使得观念是如此的活泼和生动，以至那个观念与我们从经验得来的那些推论类似。这是一个我们或许已经稍许认识的神秘的事情，在本书的进程中，我们将有更多的机会对它进行细致的探讨。
在考虑了信念对情感的影响以后，我们发现，要说明信念对想象的作用就更容易了，不管这种作用可能表现出是如何的奇特。的确，当我们的判断并不同意那些呈现于我们的想象中的意象时，我们不能从任何谈论中得到愉悦。惯于说谎的人，即使是在谈及一些无关紧要的事情，也决不能使人感到任何满足；这是因为他们呈现给我们的那些观念并不伴随有信念，因此无法在心灵中留有任何印象。诗人们尽管以说谎为职业，但他们总是努力去给他们的虚构以一种真实的模样；如果这一点被完全忽视了，
那么不管他们的作品如何具有独创性，也决不能给予我们更多的愉悦。我们可以简单地说，即使观念对意志和情感没有丝毫的影响，为了使想象对它们感到愉快，它们仍然需要真实和实在这两个条件。
但是，如果我们将出现在这个名目下的所有现象都放在一起加以比较，我们将会发现，无论“真实”在所有天才的著作中显得多么的必需，它的作用都只是使观念更容易被接受，并且使心灵乐于、或者至少是没有不情愿去遵从它们。可是，根据我的体系，

由因果关系的推理而建立的那些观念都伴随有可靠性和强力，而这些可靠性和强力又很容易就被假定为导致了上述的那种作用的产生；这样，信念对想象的所有影响都可以根据那个体系得到解释。因此，我们可以说，无论在什么情况下，如果那种影响是源自于真实或实在以外的任何其他原理，那些原理就替代了真实或实在的位置，并且给予想象以同等的愉悦。诗人们已经形成了它们所谓的诗意的事物体系，尽管这些体系既不为他们自己也不为读者们相信，它们却被公认为是任何虚构的一个充分的基础。我们已经如此地习惯了战神、天神、爱神这样的名称，以至于像教育把任何意见注入人们的心中一样，对这些观念的不断重复也使它们容易进入心灵中，并且控制想象，而不至于对判断有任何影响。
同样地，悲剧作家总是从历史中某个著名的篇章中借取它们的故事，或者至少借取它们主要角色的名字；这样做并不是为了欺骗观众，因为他们将坦白地承认，真实并不是在任何情况下都是不可侵犯地遵守的，而是为了使他们描述的非常事件更容易为想象所接受。但是，对喜剧诗人来说，这并不是必需的准备。由于喜剧诗人的人物和时间更为大家所熟悉，所以它们更容易进人构想中，并且无需任何这样的形式就可以被接受，虽然人们只要对它们一警就知道它们是虚构的，纯粹是想象的产物。
在悲剧诗人们故事中这种真伪交织的情形，不仅可以通过表明想象即使没有任何绝对的信念或担保也可以得到满足来服务于我们当下的宗旨，而且在另一种视角下也可以看作是这个体系的强有力的证明。显然，诗人们之所以采用从历史中借用它们人物的名字方法，以及史诗中的主要事件这一技巧，其目的就是为了使全部故事更容易被接受，并且使它在想象和感情上产生一个更深一249一

affections. The several incidents of the piece acquire a kind of relation
by being united into one poem or representation; and if any of these
incidents be an object of belief, it bestows a force and vivacity on the
others, which are related to it. The vividness of the first conception
diffuses itself along the relations, and is convey’ d, as by so many
pipes or canals, to every idea that has any communication with the
primary one. This, indeed, can never amount to a perfect assurance;
and that because the union among the ideas is, in a manner, acciden-
tal: But still it approaches so near, in its influence, as may convince
us, that they are deriv' d from the same origin. Belief must please the
imagination by means of the force and vivacity which attends it; since
every idea, which has force and vivacity, is found to be agreeable to
that faculty.
To confirm this we may observe, that the assistance is mutual be-
twixt the judgment and fancy, as well as betwixt the judgment and
passion; and that belief not only gives vigour to the imagination, but
that a vigorous and strong imagination is of all talents the most proper
to procure belief and authority. ' Tis difficult for us to withold our as-
sent from what is painted out to us in all the colours of eloquence;
and the vivacity produc’ d by the fancy is in many cases greater than
that which arises from custom and experience. We are hurried away by
the lively imagination of our author or companion; and even he him-
self is often a victim to his own fire and genius.
Nor will it be amiss to remark, that as a lively imagination
very often degenerates into madness or folly, and bears it a great
resemblance in its operations; so they influence the judgment after
the same manner, and produce belief from the very same princi-
ples.When the imagination，from any extraordinary ferment of the
blood and spirits, acquires such a vivacity as disorders all its pow-
ers and faculties, there is no means of distinguishing betwixt truth
and falshood; but every loose fiction or idea, having the same influ-
ence as the impressions of the memory, or the conclusions of the
judgment, 'is receiv'd on the same footing, and operates with equal

的印象。故事中的各个事件通过联结在一首诗或一个剧本中获取了一种联系；如果这些事件中的任何一个是信念的对象，它就会赋予与之相关的其他事件以一种力度和活泼性。沿着这些关系，第一个概念将自已的活泼性散布出去，并且像通过许多管道和沟渠那样，将它的活泼性传送到与原初观念有任何关联的每一个观念上。的确，这决不能算是一种完美的确信；这是因为，在某种意义上，这些观念之间的联结是偶然的。但是，就其影响而言，
它仍然是如此的接近完美，以至使得我们确信，它们是来自于同一根源。信念必然会依靠伴随它的力度和活泼性而使想象感到愉悦；因为每一个具有力度和活泼性的观念都被发现能够使那种感管能力感到愉快。
为了证明这一点，我们可以说，和判断和情感一样，判断和想象之间也是相互协助的；不仅信念会给予想象以活力，而且那种活泼和有力的想象是在一切能力中最有能力去获取信念和权威的。对我们而言，很难不去赞同任何以鲜明色彩向我们描绘出来的东西；在许多情况下，想象所产生的活泼性要比产生于习惯和经验的活泼性要更大。我们为作者或同伴的生动想象所支配，甚至作者本人也常常会成为他自已的热情和才华的牺牲品。
谈及下面的这一点将不会有错误，即正如一个生动的想象常常会堕落为疯狂或放荡，并且会产生一个与之非常类似的作用一样，想象的作用也会以同样的方式影响判断，并且根据极为相同的原理产生信念。想象由于血液和情绪的任何特别的冲动而获取如此的活泼性，以至它的全部力量和感官能力都陷人无序状态，使得我们没有任何办法区分真伪；但是每一个已经具有和记忆的印象或判断的结论相同的影响的散漫的虚构或观念都被同一251

等地看待，并且以同等的力量作用于情感。一个当下的印象和一个习惯性的过渡对激起我们的观念来说就不再是一个必要条件。
头脑中的每一个狂想，就同我们先前庄严地称之为关于事实的结论（有时也称之为感官的当下印象）的那些推论一样活泼和有力。
我们可以在诗歌中看到这种较小程度的相同作用；其中仅仅有这样的不同，也即最轻微的反省就能驱散诗歌的幻想，并且将对象置于它们的恰当视野中。然而，可以确定的是，诗人在诗意的狂热进发的时候有一个伪造的信念，甚至亲眼见到了一种他的对象似的。如果有少许论证来支持他的这种信念，那就没有什么比一个光辉的诗歌中的人物形象更能助长他的充分信念，这些人物形象不仅对他的读者，而且对诗人自已也都有作用。
